head: 98762ba53214c4f772e9ace3d5012757b524418b
method: read-first, evidence-first; 7 parallel hostile investigators + independent inline verification of all CRITICAL/HIGH claims. No production logic modified.

toolchain_run.npm_test_default: ATTEMPTED (long-running full suite; superseded by CI-config analysis as authoritative gate)

confidence_legend: PROVEN = independently verified in code by auditor this session; PLAUSIBLE = single-agent file-cited, not personally re-verified line-by-line

findings.finding: resolveServerRole() unconditionally returns "admin" for EVERY authenticated user. This defeats commit 2f551a2 ("gate high-impact approval flag behind server-verified role"): in run/route.ts the approval-flag guard resolves role=admin => canApprove always true, so any user can self-approve high-impact financial guardrails via approvalFlag:true.
findings.proof: server-role.ts returns literal "admin" after session check; no other definition exists. Verified inline.
findings.risk: Any authenticated user is treated as admin by all resolveServerRole consumers (run, override, operator, scenario, entity, value, calibration, users/roles). Self-approval of high-impact actions.
findings.required_fix: Resolve real role from getPolicyContext/UserRoleAssignment; add test asserting non-admin denied canApprove/canEdit.

findings.finding: Cross-tenant governed-decision write via POST /api/operator. Chain: (1) resolveServerRole=admin (SEC-01) passes canEdit; (2) getItems() scopes by placeholder workspaceId=session.user.id (SEC-03) so a foreign OperatorItem is not found => beforeItem undefined => entitlement/idempotency/status-transition/completion guards all skipped; (3) updateItem() runs findFirst({id}) then update({where:{id}}) with NO workspace filter; (4) DB backstop inert (SEC-04). Net: any authenticated user can mutate another workspace's OperatorItem given its UUID. Audit attributes the change to the victim, not attacker.
findings.proof: Components verified inline: always-admin (SEC-01), placeholder workspace (SEC-03), inert backstop (SEC-04). updateItem unscoped update confirmed by agent trace.
findings.risk: IDOR-gated cross-tenant write of governed decisions (status flip, mark complete with attacker outcome). Only barrier is UUID secrecy (security-by-obscurity, not a control).
findings.required_fix: Make workspaceId mandatory in updateItem/applyOverride and filter update by it; scope POST /api/operator to ctx.verifiedWorkspaceId; add cross-tenant negative test.

findings.finding: requireWorkspaceContext() returns workspaceId = session.user.id — a placeholder still wired into governed read/write paths (run, operator store, override, governance/alerts, several metrics/observability routes, audit-log). Divergent tenancy: same request carries both ctx.verifiedWorkspaceId (real) and user-id-as-workspace. Team members in the same real workspace cannot see shared data; enables SEC-02.
findings.proof: context.ts:24 `const workspaceId = session.user.id; // temporary` verified inline.
findings.risk: Data-model incoherence + isolation enabler.
findings.required_fix: Delete placeholder; derive from real membership; thread ctx.verifiedWorkspaceId into store/audit.

findings.finding: The Prisma workspace-enforcement extension is INERT. WORKSPACE_OWNED_MODELS/GLOBAL_MODELS are keyed camelCase ('engagement') but Prisma v7 passes model PascalCase ('Engagement'), so isWorkspaceOwned is always false and every operation short-circuits `if(!isWorkspaceOwned||isGlobal) return query(args)` before any check. It is registered live on the db client (db.ts:52), giving false impression of DB-level isolation. Tenant protection is therefore route-level ONLY across 317 routes with no backstop.
findings.proof: Self-documented in code comment (GAP-TEN-01); casing mismatch verified inline; registration verified inline.
findings.risk: No defense-in-depth. Any route that omits a scoping check is a silent cross-tenant leak (see SEC-02).
findings.required_fix: Normalize casing; re-classify User as membership-scoped; scope known unscoped writers (signup, audit cleanup); add test that unscoped operatorItem.update throws.

findings.finding: Commit 3dd002f ('stop trusting client x-workspace-id') only partially applied. ~30 handlers still READ x-workspace-id from the client; sampled ones are redeemed by a secondary membership check (enforceWorkspaceScoping / assertEngagementAccess) so not exploitable, but several canonical-wrapped routes (actions, findings, recommendations) ignore the already-verified ctx.verifiedWorkspaceId in favor of the header. Fragile: safety depends on every handler remembering the membership check.
findings.proof: actions route reads header then calls assertEngagementAccess (engagementMembership gate) — verified inline; the client workspaceId only narrows, cannot broaden.
findings.risk: Latent; one forgetful handler from a leak.
findings.required_fix: Standardize on ctx.verifiedWorkspaceId; reduce header reads to equality assertions.

findings.finding: Three incompatible role vocabularies coexist (admin|operator|viewer; system_admin|...|viewer; admin|operator|reviewer). users/[userId]/roles builds policy.roles from resolveServerRole()=>"admin", which is not a ROLE_HIERARCHY key => level 0 => role assignment fails closed (over-restrictive today) but is broken and one mapping change from privilege escalation.
findings.risk: Fragile; escalation risk under refactor.
findings.required_fix: Feed real ctx.policy to hierarchy; consolidate to one role model.

findings.finding: withIdempotency() in src/infra/idempotency.ts unconditionally runs the operation and returns {isNew:true} — it never reads/writes any store ('Non-DB mode: assume all operations are new'). It is imported by the core governed-mutation services (action, evidence, recommendation, engagement, findings, kpi, lead, client-account, role-assignment, business-condition, engagement-membership, user) and routes (actions, deliverables, users), several of which REQUIRE the Idempotency-Key header (fail-closed) then ignore it. The IdempotencyRecord table is dead (only referenced by generated client). A separate REAL DB-backed src/services/idempotency.ts exists (34 usages) — so coverage is split and inconsistent.
findings.proof: withIdempotency body verified inline; importer list verified via grep inline.
findings.reproduction: POST same action twice with same Idempotency-Key => two Action rows.
findings.risk: Duplicate governed mutations (double budget entry, double action). Violates CLAUDE.md hard rule.
findings.required_fix: Route governed mutations through the real services/idempotency.ts (DB-backed, P2002 race handling); scope idempotency key per workspace; delete or implement infra/withIdempotency.

findings.finding: Only ONE mutation path (applyTaskTransition, delegated tasks) writes its audit event inside the same DB transaction as the mutation. Every other governed mutation writes audit AFTER commit; core decision paths (decision-lifecycle transition, operator updateItem, applyOverride) SWALLOW audit-write failures (.catch => logger.warn) so the mutation persists with no audit record. emitAuditEvent also silently no-ops (returns 'fail-safe-no-workspace-id') when workspaceId missing. Comment 'fail-closed if audit fails' sits directly above a fail-OPEN .catch.
findings.proof: 17 exact 'Failed to emit audit event' swallow sites verified inline via grep (agent's broader .catch-around-audit count higher). Atomic applyTaskTransition pattern confirmed as the sole correct model.
findings.risk: State/audit divergence under DB pressure; violates 'all meaningful mutations must emit audit events'.
findings.required_fix: Write audit inside the mutation transaction everywhere; remove swallow .catch; make emitAuditEvent throw on missing workspaceId.

findings.finding: Audit logging is NOT centralized: 5 parallel mechanisms — infra/audit.emitAuditEvent (DB+hash chain, de-facto primary), services/audit/audit-log.logAuditEvent (DB, throws), services/audit-trail MockAuditEventStore (in-memory, dead), services/audit/log.logDecision (console.log stub), and scattered direct db.auditEvent.create. Two identically-named queryAuditEvents in different files.
findings.risk: No single choke point; per-path audit reasoning required.
findings.required_fix: Consolidate on infra/audit.emitAuditEvent; delete console/mock stubs.
findings.note: Audit READ path (GET /api/audit, /api/audit/events, /api/admin/audit-log) is PROVEN_REAL: DB-backed, workspace-scoped, capability-gated, SHA-256 hash-chain verifiable.

findings.finding: The >100000 approval-threshold workflow (canCompleteWithApprovalStatus/enforceApprovalRequirement) is enforced on exactly ONE route (/api/operator). High-impact finance/budget/decision routes (owner/budget/spend, decisions execute/accept) are gated only by a coarse capability, never by the approval workflow. resolveOwnerApproval (/api/owner/approvals/resolve) only RETURNS whether approval is needed — it mutates/gates nothing; a direct API caller skips it.
findings.risk: Material financial actions bypass owner approval by direct API call.
findings.required_fix: Enforce approval server-side inside decision-lifecycle & finance/budget mutation services; make resolveOwnerApproval a server gate.

findings.finding: /api/override writes the override justification to a process-global in-memory array (override/store.ts: `let overrideStore = []`), never persisted, lost on restart, shared across all tenants; getOverrides has no callers. The durable justification for a guardrail override exists only as a best-effort, .catch-swallowed audit event.
findings.proof: override/store.ts module-global array verified inline.
findings.risk: No durable, tenant-scoped record of why a guardrail was overridden.
findings.required_fix: Persist override records to a tenant-scoped DB model with audit.

findings.finding: Core governed transitions are last-write-wins plain update({where:{id}}) with no version/status guard: acceptDecision, rejectDecision, approveOutcomeVerification, applyOverride, operator updateItem. Transition validity is checked before the write (TOCTOU). Contrast: applyTaskTransition, transitionDecisionState, and actions/complete DO use guarded updateMany/version.
findings.proof: decision-acceptance plain update verified inline.
findings.risk: Concurrent transitions both succeed; duplicate audit events; clobbered state.
findings.required_fix: Convert to status/version-guarded updateMany with count===1 assertion.

findings.finding: Re-accept hole: validateDecisionForAcceptance allows status 'pending' OR 'in_progress' (human-decision-validator.ts:64), but acceptDecision SETS status to 'in_progress'. So an already-accepted decision (in_progress) passes validation again and can be re-accepted repeatedly — re-emitting DECISION_ACCEPTED, overwriting lastUpdatedBy, resetting updatedAt. No idempotency key, no concurrency guard. Silent re-mutation of an accepted governed record.
findings.proof: Both lines verified inline.
findings.risk: Violates 'no silent mutation of approved records'.
findings.required_fix: Allow only 'pending' in validator; status-guarded updateMany; require idempotency key on accept route.

findings.finding: Outcome 'success' is model-vs-model fabrication, not measured business metrics. accuracyScore = 100 - |confidenceImprovement - 10| (maximized when model confidence rises ~10 pts, no tie to any real KPI). actualImpact = generateBusinessImpact() (a model estimate). valueRecoveredINR = formula on impact-LEVEL strings x revenue. getEngagementOutcomes aggregates these fabricated snapshots => a business with flat/declining KPIs can display high accuracy and large 'value recovered'.
findings.risk: Owner sees false success; core proof-backed promise violated.
findings.required_fix: Ground accuracy/value in persisted KPI snapshots; flat KPIs must yield accuracy~0, value=0.

findings.finding: The core product promise 're-evaluate when outcomes do NOT improve' is NOT wired. recordOutcome computes regression but does NOT call triggerReEvaluation. The variance->replan/rollback/halt FeedbackLoop (outcome-core/feedback-loop.ts) has no production caller (only an __ignored_tests__ reference).
findings.risk: Bad outcomes never trigger governed re-evaluation. Adaptive rule violated.
findings.required_fix: In recordOutcome, on regression/low accuracy call triggerReEvaluation({changeType:'failed_implementation'|'kpi_deterioration'}); wire or delete FeedbackLoop.

findings.finding: Of 9 CLAUDE.md mandatory adaptive triggers, 4 are wired (new critical evidence, unresolved critical blocker, scope change, key employee loss), 2 partial (shock event, major client loss), 3 MISSING (kpi_deterioration only emits an alert not a re-eval; failed_implementation defined but no caller; owner_non_compliance defined but no caller). triggerReEvaluation engine itself is real & substantial. Bug: evaluateInterventionPhaseImpact blockers always [] => canAdvance always true (an unresolved critical blocker can never block phase advancement in re-eval output).
findings.risk: Key adaptive triggers never fire.
findings.required_fix: Add real callers for the 3 missing triggers; populate phase blockers.

findings.finding: createShockEvent does NOT persist the ShockEvent (comment falsely claims 'model does not exist' — it exists at schema:949). updateShockEvent is a hard stub (always throws). list/getShockEventDetail query db.shockEvent which the create path never writes => created shocks never appear.
findings.risk: Shock-event trigger path is non-functional/invisible.
findings.required_fix: Persist ShockEvent in createShockEvent; implement updateShockEvent.

findings.finding: The AI/deterministic anti-gaming precheck (runProofPrecheck/computeProofPrecheck) has ZERO runtime callers — the live submit path stops at SUBMITTED and waits for a human. tamperRisk/inconsistent signals are inputs no code computes (producers only in tests). Consequences: irrelevant evidence passes (validation only checks type match + non-empty fields); reuse caught only by exact byte-hash (re-encode => new hash => not flagged); 'freshness' measured from acceptedAt/reviewedAt (submission recency), never artifact/EXIF age (a 2-year-old photo submitted today is 'fresh').
findings.risk: Staff gaming: irrelevant/old/re-encoded evidence accepted.
findings.required_fix: Wire runProofPrecheck into intake; implement at least one real tamper/artifact-age signal.
findings.note: Positive: staff proof FSM + human-review gate + separation-of-duty + exact-hash dedup + freshness gate ARE real and wired (proof.service.ts, task-completion.service.ts). SYSTEM actor structurally cannot final-accept.

findings.finding: /api/owner/tasks/complete accepts client-supplied maxProofAgeDays (nullable). Passing null disables the freshness gate entirely; there is no server floor and the chosen threshold is not itself audited. Owner override (ownerOverride:true) also skips proof entirely (audited via OWNER_TASK_OVERRIDE_USED — a real mitigation).
findings.risk: Owner/manager can accept arbitrarily stale/no proof.
findings.required_fix: Server-side floor on maxProofAgeDays; audit any threshold override.

findings.finding: decision-evidence 'verified' is a passthrough boolean (verified: f.verified ?? false) — no verification computation. Any decision evidence can be self-declared verified.

A canned generic-advice engine is LIVE on /api/diagnosis: BASE_RECOMMENDATIONS are 6 hardcoded ungrounded business-fluff strings ('Most businesses leave 10-20% revenue on the table...'). POSTing /api/diagnosis with optional monthlyRevenue/costs/customerCount omitted defaults them to 0 and still returns all 6 canned recommendations with a personalizationScore — fabricated advice from zero data, no abstention.
findings.proof: engine.ts canned strings and diagnosis route confirmed; a SECOND real evidence-grounded consulting engine (src/services/consulting-engine/*) also exists => DUPLICATE_OR_CONFLICTING_ENGINE.
findings.risk: Owner receives generic fluff presented as diagnosis.
findings.required_fix: Route /api/diagnosis through the grounded consulting engine or gate behind data-sufficiency abstention.

findings.finding: The fine-grained abstention/danger/constraint safety gate (governance/abstention-engine.ts assessSafety) is real, substantial, unit-tested — but only runs in the benchmark harness (round2-scorer), NEVER on the owner-facing consulting write path (runConsultingPipeline persists recommendations with no assessConsultingOutput call). Worse, the benchmark adapter hardcodes several gate inputs to safe values (evidence_contradictions:0, scope_valid:true, irreversibility_score:0, operator_capacity_available:true, active_conflicts:0), so those branches can never fire.
findings.risk: Advertised bounded/proof-backed guarantees demonstrated in tests, not enforced in production.
findings.required_fix: Call assessConsultingOutput in the production pipeline with real signals; add integration test proving abstention on a constraint-conflicting memo.
findings.note: Advisory overall = PARTIALLY_CONTROLLED. No live LLM in the recommendation path (default UnavailableAiProvider fails closed); engines are deterministic rules — safe from unbounded/autonomous behavior.

findings.finding: Per-recommendation proof linkage is dropped at persistence. The diagnosis carries exact evidenceIds/rootCauseId in-memory, but createRecommendationsFromInterventions persists only title/description/impact/priority; evidenceIds/rootCauseId are discarded. Stored Recommendation instead gets an engagement-wide evidenceValidationScore. Cannot trace a persisted recommendation to the specific facts that justified it.

Subscription/rate-limit tier is read from a CLIENT-supplied x-tier header (actions/route.ts:53, tier-enforcement.ts:143, rate-limit.ts:166) and NOTHING sets x-tier server-side (grep for a setter returns nothing). A free-tier client sends x-tier:enterprise for enterprise quotas. Compounding: the store is MockRateLimitStore (in-memory, per-instance, resets on restart) so rate limiting is largely non-functional in serverless.
findings.proof: x-tier read verified inline; no server-side setter found via grep inline.
findings.risk: Tier/quota bypass.
findings.required_fix: Derive tier server-side from DB subscription; strip inbound x-tier; back rate limiting with shared store.

findings.finding: assertCapability selects currentPeriodEnd but never compares it to now(). A subscription left status:'active' with a past currentPeriodEnd (e.g. dropped renewal/cancel webhook — see WEBHOOK-01) grants full access indefinitely.
findings.note: Positive: the DB-backed assertCapability gate itself is PROVEN_REAL and fails closed (missing sub/status!=active/capability-not-in-plan/usage>=limit/any-error => deny), wired into real write routes.

findings.finding: The stripe webhook route does NOT await processing: handleWebhookEvent(event).then().catch() then immediately returns 202. In serverless the function may be frozen/killed after the response, so markWebhookEventProcessed may never run; subscription-activation events can be delayed or (after retries) dead-lettered — customer paid, never entitled. syncSubscriptionStatus fails OPEN (catches and returns while the caller marks the event processed) so a failed cancel/downgrade is silently lost. recoverStaleProcessingEvents runs a full-table scan on every webhook request.
findings.risk: Entitlement diverges from what the customer paid for.
findings.required_fix: Await processing before ack (or durable queue); do not fail-open on subscription-state writes.
findings.note: Positive: Stripe signature verification is PROVEN_REAL (raw body, constructEvent, fail-closed 401; fail-closed on missing STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET); stripeEventId @unique dedupes replay.

findings.finding: The custom replay-timestamp check is theater: verifyWebhookSignature hardcodes timestamp = Math.floor(Date.now()/1000) instead of parsing the Stripe signature t= value, so checkSignatureTimestamp always sees age~0 and can never reject. checkEventOrdering only logs, never blocks. Real replay defense comes solely from the Stripe SDK 300s tolerance + stripeEventId unique dedup.

Governed models carry NO direct workspaceId (scoped only indirectly via engagement_id): Action, Evidence, EvidenceItem, Finding, ApprovalRequest, OverrideRecord, DecisionSnapshot, IdempotencyRecord. Any query fetching these by id without joining through engagement crosses tenants. Contrast Recommendation/OperatorItem/CanonicalEvent which do carry workspace_id.
findings.proof: Action model has engagementId but no workspaceId — verified inline.
findings.required_fix: Add workspaceId + composite indexes to governed models; filter on it in every read.

findings.finding: 82 onDelete: Cascade in schema, including the Owner* governed-record tree (RecoveryFinding/RecoveryAction/RecoveryVerification and ~40 more cascade from OwnerBusiness/cycle). Deleting one OwnerBusiness hard-deletes all its findings/actions/verifications with no audit emission. Violates 'no destructive deletes for governed records' + 'all meaningful mutations must emit audit events'. Also missing User FKs on Action.assignedTo, Recommendation.approvedBy/createdBy, Evidence.submittedBy/validatedBy (bare String @db.Uuid).
findings.proof: 82 cascade count + ClientAccount workspace FKs verified inline.
findings.required_fix: Change governed cascades to Restrict + soft-delete + audit; add User FK relations.

findings.finding: Multiple models have a column named workspaceId whose FK points to ClientAccount, not Workspace: PrivateModeAccess (schema:3464), OwnerInputRecord (3489), OwnerInputQualityAssessment (3515), plus WorkspaceActionOutcomes/ReassessmentEvents/ControlledLearning* relations (3549,3581,3611,3641). A column named workspace_id referencing client_accounts.id is an entity collapse; any code joining these to the real Workspace on workspaceId is wrong. Violates 'no collapsing distinct entities'.
findings.proof: FK targets verified inline (workspace ClientAccount @relation fields:[workspaceId]).
findings.required_fix: Rename/repoint these fields to clientAccountId.

findings.finding: Nearly every governed status is a free-form String (no enum/CHECK): Action.status, Subscription.status, Recommendation.status, Finding.status, ApprovalRequest.approvalStatus, WebhookEvent.status, Evidence.status. Nullable critical columns allow contradictory states: Recommendation.status='approved' with approvedBy/approvedAt NULL; Evidence validated with validatedBy/validatedAt NULL; ApprovalRequest approved with approvedAt NULL. Only EvidenceItem uses real enums (pattern exists, not applied). AuditEvent.workspaceId and previousHash are nullable => tenant-less audit + resettable hash chain.
findings.required_fix: Convert governed statuses to enums; add partial/CHECK constraints tying terminal status to required fields; make audit workspaceId/hash non-null.

findings.finding: The primary nav landing /dashboard is a server component that fetches its OWN API by absolute URL (NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL ?? http://localhost:3000/api/engagements) with NO cookie forwarding. Server-side fetch carries no session cookie => withCanonicalEnforcement 401 => every helper `return []`. An owner with real engagements/findings/actions sees 0 everywhere and the 'Run your first diagnosis' empty-state. The single most-visited screen is a false-empty.
findings.proof: fetch-without-cookies pattern verified inline (4 self-fetches, return [] on !res.ok).
findings.risk: Primary screen always blank; owner concludes nothing exists.
findings.required_fix: Call services directly in the server component or forward cookies() into fetch.

findings.finding: Top-level /decisions ('Decision Inbox / Review, approve, and govern decisions') renders DecisionInboxTable which fetches the wrong endpoint (/api/governance/metrics) and then hardcodes setDecisions([]) — it can never show a decision. A SECOND, real inbox exists at /dashboard/inbox (fetches /api/decisions/list) but is not linked anywhere in nav. The fake one owns the pretty URL.
findings.proof: setDecisions([]) verified inline.
findings.required_fix: Point /decisions at the working InboxClient or redirect to /dashboard/inbox.

findings.finding: The persistent sidebar (ui/shell/sidebar-nav.tsx NAV_ITEMS) has only 10 links; ~30 owner/operator pages that ARE operational (owner/home, owner/finance..wealth, my-day, diagnosis, control, value) are NOT in the sidebar — reachable only by typed URL or a one-time post-onboarding redirect. The only owner nav item (/owner/recovery) has zero outbound links. The owner journey pieces are individually operational but the ASSEMBLY is broken — an owner cannot walk diagnose->decide->assign->track->verify using the app's own navigation.
findings.required_fix: Wire owner command center into sidebar gated on OWNER_VIEW; add outbound links from /owner/recovery.
findings.note: Positive: owner/finance domain spine (create business, snapshot, run diagnosis, assign/start/complete/block action, verify outcome) IS operational and persists; owner/home renders honest 'no data'/'unknown' states.

findings.finding: engagements/[id]/experiments/[experimentId]/approve/route.ts uses 'Mock store for now - would fetch from DB in production'. Owner-reachable via the engagement experiments surface. Violates CLAUDE.md 'no stubs'.
findings.proof: Comment verified inline.

findings.finding: api/public/engagements, /actions, /kpis return hardcoded mock arrays (mockEngagements/mockActions/mockKPIs).
findings.proof: Verified inline.

findings.finding: Four large mock-data-generator components (execution-workspace-shell, portfolio-command-center-shell, admin-billing-shell, self-serve-onboarding-shell) are imported by nothing. Would render fabricated healthy portfolios/billing if ever routed (latent MISLEADING risk).

97 test files live in src/__ignored_tests__/ and are globally excluded from vitest (vitest.config.ts exclude '**/__ignored_tests__/**') — they run in NO lane (not even the visible quarantine lane). They include critical-sounding names: workspace-isolation-enforcement.test.ts, owner-dashboard.test.tsx, recommendation.test.ts, root-cause-engine.test.ts, decision-control.service.test.ts. Some correspond to removed dead subsystems; others sound live. Any behavior they claimed to cover is untested in CI.
findings.proof: 97 count + exclude glob verified inline.
findings.required_fix: Triage: re-enable live-behavior tests, delete dead-subsystem tests; nothing critical should be dark.

findings.finding: ci.yml runs a real DB suite with TEST_WITH_DB=true but EXCLUDES 23 quarantined files (52 failing tests) from the BLOCKING lane (visible non-blocking lane only). Two are security-relevant and report REAL defects: phase-i10-enforcement-scanner.test.ts ('14 UNWRAPPED routes lacking withEnforcement') and security/route-scanner.test.ts ('unprotected routes outside exemption registry'); plus security/ops-endpoints-auth.test.ts and security/diagnostic-key-validation.test.ts fail collection (0 tests), and signup-schema-contract ('owner OWNER_VIEW capability contract fails'). So the product ships with the codebase's own scanners red, gated to non-blocking.
findings.proof: quarantine.json contents + ci.yml lanes verified inline.
findings.required_fix: Fix the 14 unwrapped routes (or prove genuine exemption) and un-quarantine the security scanners into the blocking lane.

findings.finding: The default `npm test` (no TEST_WITH_DB) additionally excludes all *.integration.test.ts (14), *.placeholder.test.ts (1), phase-*.test.ts (21), runtime-proof/** (11), and every [db]-tagged test (94 files) via testNamePattern. So a developer running `npm test` locally exercises a much smaller surface than CI. CI itself does set TEST_WITH_DB=true (good).
findings.proof: Counts verified inline.

findings.finding: ACTIVE tests counted in the '13,994 passing' figure assert constants under governance-guarantee names. Verified: api/decisions.test.ts (header 'Tier 1 critical invariants: workspace isolation, auth, state machine, audit') has 50 `expect(true).toBe(true)` and 37 empty bodies tagged TODO_A2_FAKE_TEST_QUARANTINED; business-condition-workspace-isolation.test.ts 'should throw Unauthorized for cross-workspace access' asserts `"ws_123" !== "ws_456"`; the 12-file api/owner/learning-* cluster vi.mock the service AND @/lib/db then assert the mock. The team's own .claude/A2_FAKE_TEST_INVENTORY.md self-documents '614 quarantined fakes' left inline in active files. Also 59 files gate real assertions behind describe.skipIf(!SHOULD_RUN_DB_TESTS) so local `npm test` executes zero of those assertions; operator-route.real.test.ts has 5/5 bodies it.skip'd.
findings.proof: 50 expect(true) + 37 TODO markers + ws_123!==ws_456 + 614-fakes inventory all verified inline.
findings.risk: Pass count is materially inflated; governance-named tests prove nothing.
findings.required_fix: Delete/replace the 614 documented fakes with real service-boundary tests; make DB lane the default local run.
findings.note: Mitigating: ci.yml required PR gate DOES run TEST_WITH_DB=true against real Postgres, and a genuine real-DB tier exists (intervention-route.rbac, owner-business-isolation.db, decision-transition-toctou.db). False confidence is concentrated in local runs + quarantine + __ignored_tests__.

findings.finding: audit-wrapped-handlers reports 29 wrapped route files calling Response.json() directly instead of the canonical JSON response (bypassing canonical telemetry/shape). A CI ratchet prevents NEW violations but 29 pre-exist.
findings.proof: Ran `node scripts/audit-wrapped-handlers.js audit` => 29 violations.
